what: Snap-on makes professional tools. Its best-known business sells high-end hand tools and diagnostic equipment to vehicle mechanics from vans that visit workshops weekly, often financed by Snap-on's own credit arm.
customers: Vehicle repair technicians and workshops, plus aerospace, military, mining and manufacturing customers.
money: hand tools and tool storage sold through the mobile van network
diagnostic equipment, repair data and workshop equipment
tools for aerospace, military and industry
moat: A franchised van network that visits mechanics at work every week, builds personal relationships and extends credit, which no catalogue or online seller replicates.
risks: Technicians defer buying expensive tools when their own income is uncertain
Revenue grew only about 1% last year
Credit losses in its financing arm rise in downturns
Electric vehicles need different and in some cases fewer tools
opportunities: Operating margin of 26% and return on invested capital of 14%
A dividend yield around 2.7% with a long record of increases
Cash exceeds debt, unusual for a company with a lending arm
watch: Tools Group organic sales and credit quality in the finance arm.
